P1.evidence: Full four-part frame delivered: 'dive in, get a good... of where we're at, like really clear understanding where we're trying to get to with fitness and just figure out what's kind of missing, what we need to fill in, and then from there we can map out what it might look like to work with Trevor. Does that all sound good?' Open question followed: 'What do you feel we can potentially help you with?' Application was only referenced in passing later ('I think I saw it from your application, you're 48 right now'), not read back at the open.

P2.evidence: Only health conditions were actually asked: 'Have you noticed any health stuff pop up the last couple years?' Age was confirmed from the application; height (5'9") and weight (190) were volunteered, never asked. Injuries were never asked — the prospect volunteered a crush injury that nearly cost him his foot and the rep did not ask one follow-up question about it. No training week, no results, no diet questions, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: Good bridge to motivation: 'I want a bit more clarity on kind of the motivation behind it as well... what are some other kind of motivations or drives behind actually handling this right now, man?' Strong 'can't do it now' work on spearfishing — 'I don't 100% feel confident shooting a fish that I used to.' Clean reflect-back: 'getting into shape isn't just... a lot of this is just about actually being able to do the things that you want to do long-term' → 'Exactly.' Never asked who else it impacts; the girlfriend came up as rapport, not as a deep-goal lever, and kids/legacy/identity were never driven through.

P4.evidence: 'What had you fall off, man? I mean, by, you know, being in the best shape of your life to kind of downward spiral, like what actually, what happened?' and 'What do you think has been holding you back? Like what's been missing from you getting back on the wagon with all this?' Prospect named work hours and boredom with gym training as the gap. The rep never ran the 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?' line, so the structural root cause was left implicit.

P5.evidence: Consequence question run close to script: 'let's say we don't make a pivot here. Like, what is the next two, three, four or five years look like for you if we continue in this direction?' Prospect gave a strong answer ('I will stop doing the things that I love'). Rep then jumped straight to 'Sounds like it might be time to draw a line in the sand' as a statement rather than asking whether he was willing to settle and why not, so the frame was never deepened.

P6.evidence: Commitment check run before the price: 'provided we can figure out the logistics... do you really feel like, hey, dude, now's the time to go all in, commit to the workouts, like, follow the protocol, and get into the best shape of your life again?' Got a yes before quoting $6,000. The belief question ('can you get there with the right structure and right person') only appeared afterwards as part of the money isolate.

P11.evidence: Price was presented but the money objection ended the call before any payment step; no payment, no Trevor onboarding call, no agreement email, no Skool/welcome-email instructions.

objection_plays.detail: Isolate ran ('finances aside, though, like, you do really feel like everything we covered can get you into the thing that we wanted'). 'We never want finances to be an issue' and the payment plan/financing invitation ran. Of the financial picture the script asks for, only credit score was asked ('I was going to ask, how's your credit score?') — cash on hand, monthly surplus after bills, number of credit cards, available vs used credit and investments were all skipped. The rep then abandoned the play and parked the call: 'maybe let's just keep it here for now.' The 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' reframe never ran.

notes: Discovery-to-consequence work was genuinely good but Baseline was almost entirely skipped — and the check the rep skipped hardest (injuries) is the one this prospect most needed, given a crushed pelvis and a near-amputated foot that are symptomatic again. On the money objection he ran the isolate and then quit after one question; the full financial picture was never taken, so 'can't afford it' was accepted at face value rather than tested.
